clean_message: Hi, I heard about your mushrooms from a friend and wanted to try. Can I pick up a small mixed box tomorrow morning in Kreuzberg, something for two people, vegetarian. I don't eat dairy, please keep that in mind. Let me know price and where exactly to come.

Hello, do you also deliver inside Berlin or only pickup. I'd like some fresh mushrooms for Sunday lunch, maybe 500g of whatever is good now. Can you tell me what you have and until what time I can collect today or tomorrow.

Order via contact form: "Mushroom Mood Today – feeling tired, need something grounding." Customer asks for enough for 3 people and no onions. Please confirm if available today and send payment details; customer mentions they can come by bike around 11–12.

Hi, quick question: do you already have forest mushrooms from around Berlin or still only cultivated ones. I'd like one box "for a cozy dinner with my partner", your choice. I can pick up on Friday after work, is 18:30 okay for you.

SMS: "Hey, it's Lukas from Neukölln, you sold me that mix last month." He asks if there is any chance for a small evening delivery because he finishes late shift at 22:00. You reply that today is not possible, suggest Saturday morning pickup and ask him to text quantity by Friday.

Email subject: "Need something warming?" Customer writes they are low energy and mostly plant-based, and ask what you recommend from what you have right now. They say budget is around 20 EUR and ask if you can pack it in two separate paper bags. Please answer with what's realistic from current stock.

Hi, I found your card at a yoga studio. Are you doing regular weekly boxes or only one-time orders. I'd like to try a small box every Sunday for April, pickup in Friedrichshain. Can we test next week and then decide on a rhythm.

Customer via email: "Today I feel a bit anxious, not hungry but know I should eat." They ask for something very light, gluten-free, for one person. Please see if you have any gentle options ready from today's harvest and reply with pickup slot before 13:00.

Short message: "Hi, same as last time but for 5 people, friends visiting from Hamburg." They ask if wild mushrooms are already in season and if you can add some herbs that help with digestion. Customer can pick up at your place tomorrow between 17–18 if you confirm.

Customer asks if you will be open the week between Christmas and New Year. They had one box in October and say it helped them feel calmer in the evenings. They want to order again for two adults, no alcohol-based ingredients, and ask if you can prepare something they can store for a few days.

Email: "Hi Mushroom House, are you still working in winter?" Customer asks what you can currently source locally and if anything is good for someone with sensitive stomach. They mention they live in Prenzlauer Berg and can only pick up before 9:30 on weekdays. Please confirm if tomorrow is possible and what amount.

Contact form: "Mood today: a bit scattered, need focus for work." They ask for a small portion for one, vegetarian, and say they like more earthy flavors, not too strong herbs. You need to reply with available varieties today and propose a pickup window after 17:00.

SMS from repeat customer: "Too hot to eat much, but want something light." They ask if you have anything that doesn't require long cooking and is okay to eat late at night. You respond with what's left from today's harvest and suggest pickup in the next hour before you close.

Hi, I met you at Markthalle Neun last weekend and loved your explanation about mood-based food. I'd like to book a small private order for next Sunday, for 3 people, no garlic, we all have early work Monday so nothing too heavy. Please let me know if you're harvesting that day and what the approximate price would be.

Customer email: They say they feel low energy before winter and ask for a "supportive" mix, mentioning they are lactose-intolerant and don't eat meat. They ask if you can label the bags with simple notes like "evening" or "lunch suitable". Confirm if your schedule allows pickup on Friday night after 20:00.

New client writes that a therapist recommended your service. They ask how to describe their mood and body needs so you can choose mushrooms and herbs. They want a trial for one week, three small portions, and ask if bank transfer is okay.

Email: "Hi, I want to surprise my partner with something from the forest." They mention vegetarian, no soy, and say they both feel a bit run down from work. You should answer what's growing right now around Berlin and whether you can prepare something for Saturday afternoon pickup.

Short note from previous customer: "Can you repeat the mix from last July, but double quantity." They add that one guest is allergic to nuts, so please avoid any nut-based additions. You reply to confirm you remember the order and ask if they need it Friday or Saturday.

Customer sends: "Feeling very grounded today, want something to match that, for two." They live in Kreuzberg and ask if you can meet near Görlitzer Park on your way back from the forest. Ask them to confirm time window and whether they prefer cash or transfer.

Last-minute order: "Anything left for New Year's Eve, not too heavy, for 4 people." They mention two guests don't drink alcohol and one is vegan. You answer that supplies are limited and propose a reduced portion for 3–4, pickup before 14:00 on the 31st.

Subject: "Weekly box idea?" Customer who ordered twice last year proposes a regular Monday morning pickup on their way to the office. They ask if you can keep it around 15 EUR each week and adapt to how they report feeling. Please reply with what is feasible for you in February and March.

Cafe owner from Neukölln writes: they tasted your mushrooms at a friend's dinner and wonder if you can supply a small brunch place. They ask what a weekly standing order for weekends could look like, maybe 3–4 kg total. You should respond with rough seasonal availability and minimum order amounts.

Quick SMS: "We're the couple from last Sunday, can we get the same mix, but 1.5 kg this time." They say friends are visiting and one guest doesn't like very strong flavors. You confirm you can do 1 kg of the same style and 0.5 kg milder, pickup at 10:30.

Restaurant inquiry: "Small bistro in Friedrichshain looking for seasonal mushrooms 2x per week." They ask if you can deliver early mornings before 8:00 and if invoices are possible monthly. Ask them what volume they expect and whether they need fixed varieties or are open to a changing selection.

Existing private customer writes that they've been ordering from you since 2012 and now want to place a bigger order for a family gathering. They ask for enough for 8–10 people, two vegan, one with celiac. You reply that you can prepare separate labeled bags and suggest pickup the evening before due to next-day forest schedule.

Early-morning WhatsApp from new hotel contact: they heard from a bistro that you supply special mushrooms. They ask if you could send a sample box this Friday for the chef to test, 2–3 kg mixed, with a simple list of what's inside. Confirm if you can deliver to Mitte at 09:00.

Email: "Recurring order request – Cafe Sonnenweg." The cafe asks if you can provide a fixed 2 kg every Saturday, with the flexibility to go up to 4 kg when they message you by Thursday. They note they prefer varieties that work for brunch and mostly vegetarian guests. Please confirm pricing and if this fits into your winter routine.

Long-time private customer writes: "Mood today: hopeful but tired, need something simple after work." They ask for a small order for one, pickup at 19:30 near Kottbusser Tor if you are passing through. You reply that you can bring a compact selection and ask them to send 10 EUR via transfer afterward.

Bistro owner: "We want to test a seasonal mushroom brunch every Sunday in May." They ask for a weekly delivery of 3 kg on Saturday mornings and want to keep the supplier local and flexible. You ask about their kitchen constraints, confirm that you can adjust varieties week by week, and suggest a check-in after two Sundays.

Customer note via webshop: "Mushroom Mood Today – I feel scattered from heat, want something calming." They select the "surprise me" option and write that they're vegan and avoid wheat. Confirm order for 2 portions, mention that delivery is not possible in this heat, and suggest pickup the next morning before temperatures rise.

New contact: small coffee shop in Kreuzberg asks if you can supply small amounts for a weekend special, maybe just 1–2 kg mixed each Friday. They say storage is limited, so they need very fresh delivery. You answer that Friday morning drops are possible after your forest round and ask for their exact opening time.

Existing bistro writes: "Guests keep asking about the mushroom guy, can we have a little story card on the table." They also confirm they will need 5 kg this weekend instead of 3 due to a group booking. You accept the increased order but mention that some varieties are limited this week and you may need to substitute with more robust ones.

Hotel contact emails: "New Year's Eve menu – final confirmation." They ask if you can still deliver 6 kg on the 30th, split into two crates, labeled for different dishes. You respond that 5 kg is realistic because of weather and foraging limits, and ask if they can adjust their menu portion sizes slightly.

Webshop order: returning customer chooses "winter support" option and writes in note: "Low energy, sleeping badly, no meat, no lactose." They ask for 3 portions for the week and mention they can only pick up after 20:00. You confirm preparation for today and ask them to ring the downstairs bell when they arrive.

Email from small restaurant: "Thursday delivery issue." They say last week's box arrived 30 minutes late and ask if you can make tomorrow's delivery strictly before 11:00, as lunch prep suffered. You reply that you'll adjust your route and confirm 10:30 drop-off, also asking if the current mix is working or needs tweaking.

Cafe Sonnenweg sends: "Same as last Sunday, plus 1 kg extra if possible." They mention guests responded well to the current mix and ask if you can keep the flavors mild. You confirm total 4 kg, explain that one variety is out this week, and propose an alternative with similar texture.

Private customer writes that they feel overwhelmed from work and want a steady weekly order for the next month. They ask for one box every Wednesday, pickup at your place after 19:00, always vegetarian and low on heavy spices. You agree to a four-week trial and ask them to send a short note each week about how they feel so you can adjust.

Restaurant in Mitte: "Can we lock in a standing order for October–November." They request 8 kg every Friday, with the option to cancel one week in advance if bookings drop. You answer that this is possible but warn that heavy storms may reduce forest yield, and ask for a backup plan if quantities need to be reduced by 20–30%.

Hotel kitchen emails about Christmas week: they want to repeat last year's order, same distribution between breakfast and dinner service. They ask if you can pre-label boxes "breakfast" and "dinner" to simplify storage. You confirm, mention a small price adjustment due to rising costs, and ask them to confirm acceptance.

Webshop ticket: customer asks whether your products are certified organic and if any items may trigger histamine issues. They want to order but need clarity on sourcing and handling. You respond with a short explanation of your forest-based supply, your handling practices, and suggest a smaller test order first.

Cafe owner writes on WhatsApp: "Hey, mood is very positive in the cafe, guests ask for seasonal specials." They want to try a special board every weekend in May and ask for an extra 2 kg on top of the usual order. You reply with "ok, starting next Friday," and ask if they want a more energizing or calming profile overall.

Email from small catering company: they are planning a vegetarian menu for a yoga retreat and need 10–12 kg over three days. They ask how far in advance you need final numbers and if you can store part of the order in your space overnight. You answer that you can split delivery, but need 5 days notice for final quantities.

Bistro in Friedrichshain: "Autumn menu adjustments." They say guests like the current mushrooms but some find them too intense for lunch. They ask if you can adjust the mix to be slightly lighter while keeping the same total quantity. You propose replacing one heavier variety with a milder one and ask for feedback after the next weekend.

Private customer note: "Mushroom Mood Today – feeling heavy, want clarity." They request enough for two meals for one person, vegan, with something that doesn't disturb sleep. You send back available options and suggest pickup after 16:00, reminding them to bring their own container if possible.

Hotel contact: "NYE final numbers changed." They now expect 20% more guests and ask if you can stretch tomorrow's delivery from 6 kg to 7.5 kg. You reply that you can add 1 kg but not more, given weather and forest conditions, and they agree to adjust portions.

New restaurant in Kreuzberg: "Trial order request." They heard about you through another chef and want a one-time 4 kg mixed box this Friday. They specify one guest has severe nut allergy and ask you to confirm there is no cross-contact with nut products in your handling. You confirm your process and ask for delivery time window.

Returning private customer sends webshop note: "Planning an easy weekend, feeling calm but low energy." They choose 3-portion box and mention they avoid gluten and strong stimulants like coffee. You confirm order and ask if Sunday morning pickup works better than Saturday evening due to your schedule.

Cafe Sonnenweg: "Summer adjustment." They explain brunch bookings dip in heat, so they want to reduce weekly order from 4 kg to 2.5 kg until August. You accept, note the new baseline, and offer to add a last-minute 1 kg if they text by Friday noon.

Small hotel emails: guests responded very well to last weekend's mushrooms and they want to integrate you into their regular breakfast concept. They propose a fixed standing order of 3 kg twice a week, with a monthly review. You respond that this is possible starting mid-September and suggest a three-month test phase.

Bistro requests "autumn special focus" for October, asking if you can lean the mix more toward deeper, earthier flavors. They still want 5 kg per week, but ask for a bit more variety to build a small tasting plate. You confirm that forest conditions allow for more diversity now and ask them to send guest feedback each week.

WhatsApp from long-term restaurant partner: "Minus 2 kg this week please, bookings dropped." They also mention a new chef started and would like to meet you once to understand your philosophy. You accept the reduced quantity and propose a quick meeting after next Friday's delivery.

Webshop customer: "Gift order for a friend going through a hard time." They ask for something gentle, vegetarian, and not too experimental, to be picked up by the friend directly. You request the friend's contact details, clarify dietary constraints, and propose a pickup window on Saturday.

Restaurant in Mitte: "Christmas rush – emergency top-up possible?" They underestimated demand and ask for an extra 2–3 kg for the 24th dinner service. You check inventory and reply that you can provide 1.5 kg this time, offering to deliver early morning on the 24th before heading to family.

Standing partner cafe requests a summary of their 2018 orders for accounting. They also ask if you are planning any price changes for 2019. You send a short recap of monthly volumes and confirm a small price increase starting March, offering to keep January–February at old rates.

New yoga studio contacts you: they want a small regular order for Sunday brunch events, about 1.5 kg per week. They stress that many guests are vegan and prefer gentle flavors. You propose a one-month trial with flexible quantities and ask whether they have refrigeration capacity for leftovers.

Webshop note from long-time customer: "Mood today: focused, stable, want to support that." They select a 4-portion box and remind you they can't tolerate garlic and onions. You confirm preparation for tonight and schedule pickup for 19:00, asking them to confirm if they are running late.

Restaurant partner writes: "Due to extreme heat, guests are eating less." They want to reduce next two deliveries by 30% and ask if that's okay on short notice. You accept, explain that forest growth is low anyway, and propose revisiting normal quantities in September.

Hotel sends: "Autumn brunch concept live from next week." They ask to switch from ad-hoc orders to a fixed weekly cycle, 4 kg every Thursday, with a soft option for +/- 1 kg depending on occupancy. You confirm and note internally to check in after three weeks on variety and guest reactions.

Catering company: "December schedule confirmation." They list three events and proposed quantities (6 kg, 8 kg, 5 kg) and ask if you can support all of them. You answer that you can meet the first two fully but need to cap the third at 4 kg; they agree and adjust menus.

Webshop customer: "Boost immunity?" They ask if you have anything supportive for this time of year, mention they work in a hospital and have irregular hours. You propose a flexible pickup window this week and suggest they order smaller portions more frequently so they don't keep anything too long.

Restaurant in Kreuzberg writes that due to restrictions they have shifted to takeaway only and reduced menu. They want to keep working with you but reduce deliveries to 50% for the next month. You agree, offer to combine their box with another client's route to save time, and propose revisiting volumes at the end of April.

Private customer: "Back to ordering after a long break." They mention stress and sleep issues, still vegetarian, and ask if your offering changed. You explain you're now focusing more on stable weekly cycles with partners but still keep a small quota for custom orders, and propose one box every two weeks as a starting point.

Hotel partner: "Occupancy slowly rising." They ask if you can return to original 2019 quantities from next week, 4 kg Thursday, 3 kg Sunday. You confirm, mention forest conditions look good, and ask if the breakfast team wants any specific texture changes for the new menu.

Bistro reports that evening business is unstable again and they might cancel a delivery on short notice. They ask how late they can decide without causing you problems. You answer that cancellations up to 24 hours before delivery are okay, but same-day changes will likely still be charged partially.

Several regulars send quick messages asking if you have "anything left at all" for New Year. You log that private capacity is full and reply with a standard message: no more boxes possible, all stock reserved for long-term partners. You suggest they check in again mid-January when forest and schedule reset.

Email from long-term cafe: they want to align their menu with your current seasonal reality. They ask you to send a short note every Monday with what's strong, what's limited, and what's not available. You agree to a simple three-line weekly email and integrate it into your Monday routine.

Private customer: "Monthly subscription idea." They propose a pre-paid package for four months, one box per month, to avoid scheduling stress. You reply that this is possible if they accept that box size may vary slightly with the season, and they agree.

Yoga retreat organizer: "Second retreat this year." They want the same pattern as last time but with more options for gluten-free participants. You confirm dates, propose similar total quantity, and ask if they can provide final attendee numbers at least 7 days before.

Restaurant writes via WhatsApp: "September menu lock." They plan a new menu and ask if they can rely on 7–8 kg every Friday for four weeks. You answer "ok, 7 kg guaranteed, 8 kg if forest allows," and add an internal note to prioritize this partner in case of scarcity.

Webshop user: "Mood today: anxious, overthinking, need something grounding for evenings." They mark themselves as repeat customer and reference an order ID from 2019. You pull up the old notes, keep similar direction but adapt to current stock, and confirm pickup for Wednesday.

Hotel partner: "Brunch numbers higher than expected this Advent." They request 1 kg extra on the next three deliveries and ask you to invoice everything together in January. You agree but flag that if heavy snow hits, you may need to lower the last delivery slightly.

New specialty coffee shop: "Trial collaboration." They ask for a small box weekly for two months to test a brunch plate, 1–1.5 kg, and mention a mostly vegetarian audience. You propose 1.5 kg for the first two weeks, then adjustment based on sales, and ask if Saturday morning delivery is okay.

Private customer returns after a year pause: "Need something steady for the next weeks, mood very unstable." They ask for small weekly boxes, always plant-based, with minimal stimulation. You suggest a four-week cycle with check-ins and remind them you cannot give medical advice, only adjust based on their feedback.

Restaurant in Mitte: "Brunch capacity up." They ask to increase Thursday delivery from 5 kg to 7 kg for June and July. You confirm June is possible, but ask to keep July flexible as last summer's heat impacted availability.

Bistro message: "Heat again, please reduce." They report guests are choosing lighter options and want to temporarily cut their weekly order in half. You adjust their profile to 2.5 kg, note "heat mode," and tell them you'll ping them in early September to see if they want to go back up.

Hotel: "Autumn packages launched." They want to coordinate mushroom deliveries with their wellness weekends and send you dates through December. You map their dates against your calendar and confirm which ones you can fully cover, marking two weekends as "reduced quantity only."

Long-term private customer: "End-of-year box?" They ask for something very simple for two evenings, vegetarian, low effort, to carry them through busy days. You say you can prepare one medium box for pickup on the 23rd, but all later slots are for partners only.

Cafe Sonnenweg: "2023 baseline." They propose 3 kg every Saturday as standard, with the option to add 1 kg for special events when they text you by Thursday noon. You agree, note the new baseline in your sheet, and ask if they want their usual calmer flavor profile to continue.

Webshop customer: "Mood today: restless but hopeful." They're mostly plant-based and ask for enough for four small meals. You recognize their email as a previous client from 2018, keep similar general direction, and propose pickup Tuesday evening, reminding them to message if anything in their body changed since last time.

Restaurant partner: "Summer menu planning." They ask you to estimate realistic weekly volumes June–August based on last year's heat and your current forest reading. You respond with a suggested volume curve, starting higher in June, lower in late July, and offer to adjust up or down with one week notice.

Hotel notes that breakfast is quieter during heat but dinner is busier. They ask if you can shift 1 kg per week from morning-oriented varieties to types that work better for later meals. You agree and log "dinner focus" on their profile for August.

Yoga studio: "Autumn retreat series x3." They list three weekends and ask for similar volumes as last year, but with more gluten-free-friendly options. You confirm total amounts, propose dividing each weekend's delivery into two smaller drops, and ask if they can store them separately.

Private customer: "Recurring Tuesday box?" They'd like a small box every Tuesday for the rest of the year, always plant-based, low stimulation, with a short note from you about when in the day it fits best. You accept with the condition that quantities may shift slightly around holidays; they agree.

Restaurant: "January forecast." They expect lower bookings and want to temporarily reduce their Friday order from 6 kg to 4 kg. You acknowledge, set the new quantity for January, and schedule a check-in call for the last week of the month to decide on February.

New specialty cafe in Prenzlauer Berg: "Intro order." They want a small box every second week to test a weekend plate, around 1 kg, vegetarian focus. You accept, propose alternating weeks to fit your route, and ask them to send a brief sales report after each weekend.

Hotel partner: "Wellness package update." They are adding a new 3-day package and ask if you can ensure slightly more grounding options on those weekends. You adjust their calendar, mark the wellness dates, and confirm that total monthly volume stays the same but distribution shifts.

Bistro: "July heat plan." They ask you to preemptively reduce their weekly order by 25% during potential heat spikes, without them needing to write each time. You agree on simple rules: if forecast exceeds a certain temperature, you lower their volume and send them a quick confirmation message.

Long-term cafe: "Autumn reset." They want to bring back a richer weekend special and ask you to dial the mix a bit deeper and more grounding, same total weight. You confirm change from next delivery and note a reminder to ask for feedback after two weekends.

Webshop customer: "Support for dark season." They're repeat and state they feel unfocused and low motivation, ask for a 3-portion box, vegan, easy to handle after late work. You confirm and schedule pickup Thursday, adding a note not to overload them with too much quantity at once.

Restaurant partner: "New chef, same agreement?" The new chef writes to confirm ongoing Friday deliveries and asks for a short overview of how you usually adapt to mood/season and bookings. You send a concise explanation, list typical autumn vs spring differences, and propose a quick call before the next menu change.

Yoga retreat organizer: "Yearly plan." They propose fixed dates for three retreats and want to lock in approximate volumes now to secure your capacity. You agree, block the dates in your calendar, and clarify that exact kg numbers will be confirmed 10 days before each retreat.

Hotel sends a short message: "For June keep everything like last year, same weeks, same amounts." They add that guest feedback was strong and they don't want to experiment too much this season. You copy last year's pattern into this year's sheet and only adjust one week due to a personal conflict.

Cafe Sonnenweg: "Autumn special board." They ask for 1 kg extra for the next four Saturdays to support a small autumn plate, and mention many guests now recognize your name. You confirm the extra weight and ask them to track which days sell out fastest.

Private customer: "End-of-year rhythm." They want two small boxes over the holidays, not too heavy, mostly plant-based, to keep a gentle structure in chaotic days. You accept but tell them exact pickup times will be tighter than usual due to partner commitments.

Restaurant in Mitte: "Q1 pattern." They propose a flat 6 kg every Friday January–March, with the option to cancel once per month without penalty. You agree, note the condition, and remind them that in case of extreme weather you may need to lower one delivery and will prioritize them in the next week.

Webshop customer from 2014 reappears: "Back in Berlin, need your help again." They describe feeling ungrounded after moving and want a small weekly box for at least a month, always vegetarian, no onions. You suggest starting bi-weekly for two cycles to see how it fits their schedule, then decide together.

Hotel partner: "Spring brunch relaunch." They want to synchronize their marketing with your current forest reality and ask for a short seasonal sentence they can print next to the buffet. You provide a practical one-line description focused on locality and season, and confirm their usual Thursday and Sunday deliveries continue unchanged.

Cafe Sonnenweg sends quick WhatsApp: "Same as last weeks, plus 0.5 kg if forest allows." They mention the mood in the cafe is calmer and guests keep asking when you'll visit again. You confirm 3.5 kg for Saturday, note to pass by for a short check-in, and mark their profile unchanged for now.
